{{Recipe}}

This recipe is for a traditional miso soup. [[Cookbook:Wakame|Wakame]] with [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]] is a standard and popular combination, especially at restaurants.

== Ingredients ==

=== Broth ===
* 90–94% by volume [[Cookbook:Dashi|dashi]] (consider using instant dashi mix)
* 6–10% by volume [[Cookbook:Miso|miso]] (red, white, or a combination)

=== Garnish ===
Any 2–3 of the following items that contrast in color, flavor, buoyancy, shape, texture, etc:

* Finely sliced and [[Cookbook:Deep Fat Fry|deep-fried]] [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]] (agedashi tofu)
* Cubed raw silky [[Cookbook:Tofu|tofu]] ('''recommended''')
* [[Cookbook:Wakame|Wakame]] seaweed ('''recommended''')
* [[Cookbook:Konbu|Konbu]] (kelp), perhaps left over from making dashi
* [[Cookbook:Spinach|Spinach]]
* Sliced [[Cookbook:Scallion|scallion]] ('''recommended''')
* Grated [[Cookbook:Daikon|daikon]] radish
* Boiled and finely cubed [[Cookbook:Potato|potato]]
* [[Cookbook:Clam|Clams]] (asari or shijimi)
* Grated [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplant]]
* [[Cookbook:Shrimp|Shrimp]]
* [[Cookbook:Mushroom|Mushrooms]]

== Procedure ==
# Put dashi in a pot.
# Add any garnish that needs cooking.
# Heat the dashi, letting it [[Cookbook:Simmer|simmer]] to cook any garnish that needs cooking. Do not bring to a rolling [[Cookbook:Boil|boil]], as this degrades the flavor.
# Add any garnish that does not need cooking, and remove from heat.
# Add the miso to the soup. Avoid boiling the miso; some nuances of the flavor will be lost.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* While certainly a traditional food, miso soup is also suited to modern interpretations. Using oil leftover from frying bacon and adding caramelized onion and cabbage produces a soup notably different from the traditional variety, and can add new interest to a classic dish. A small quantity of freshly ground black pepper added just before serving rounds out this method very well.
